draft: Misconception tags for every untagged wrong option (spec 23 §4). Codex A/B proposed, idea engine reviewed. For editors.

newMisconceptions.name: One differing study disproves the average
newMisconceptions.correction: Some studies found less and some found more, while the pooled average was about twice a gain.

newMisconceptions.name: An anchor fixes the answer
newMisconceptions.correction: A first number pulls a guess toward it, but the guess can differ from that number.

newMisconceptions.name: Beliefs leave evidence balanced
newMisconceptions.correction: People tend to notice information that fits their beliefs and pass over information that does not.

newMisconceptions.name: Everyone follows the crowd
newMisconceptions.correction: People differed in Asch's test; about a quarter never followed the wrong group.

newMisconceptions.name: Easy tasks resist social pressure
newMisconceptions.correction: Some people followed a wrong group even when the right answer was plain.

newMisconceptions.name: Others' tasks take less time
newMisconceptions.correction: People in the study guessed longer times for others' tasks and used past cases more.

newMisconceptions.name: Staying up beats sleeping after study
newMisconceptions.correction: Sleep after learning reduced forgetting compared with the same length of time awake.

newMisconceptions.name: Memories firm up at once
newMisconceptions.correction: A new memory firms up over time after learning.

newMisconceptions.name: Busy breaks aid memory
newMisconceptions.correction: Quiet rest after learning helped memory more than spending that time on other tasks.

newMisconceptions.name: A skipped reward is variable
newMisconceptions.correction: A reward after every fifth try is fixed; on a variable schedule, the number of tries keeps changing.

newMisconceptions.name: Surprise rewards teach fastest
newMisconceptions.correction: A reward after every try is the quickest way to teach a new act.

newMisconceptions.name: Steady rewards last longer
newMisconceptions.correction: Responses learned with uneven rewards are slower to fade when rewards stop.

newMisconceptions.name: Interest only grows the first amount
newMisconceptions.correction: Compound growth includes gains on past gains as well as on the starting amount.

newMisconceptions.name: Time alone compounds idle cash
newMisconceptions.correction: Compound growth needs gains; cash that earns nothing has no gains to build on.

newMisconceptions.name: Savings earn more than shares
newMisconceptions.correction: Cash savings have earned less than shares over time, though shares carry more risk.

newMisconceptions.name: Shares stay steady short term
newMisconceptions.correction: Share values can fall, so money needed soon usually suits a lower-risk place.

newMisconceptions.name: Small owners cannot vote
newMisconceptions.correction: Owners of shares can vote on big decisions at the firm's general meeting.

newMisconceptions.name: Longer terms raise the rate
newMisconceptions.correction: A longer term can raise total interest even when the loan rate stays fixed.

newMisconceptions.name: Every EMI rupee is interest
newMisconceptions.correction: An EMI can pay both interest and part of the loan sum.

newMisconceptions.name: Scanning a QR can get you money
newMisconceptions.correction: A QR scan and UPI PIN can make a payment; getting money needs neither.

newMisconceptions.name: Nuts have less fat than dal
newMisconceptions.correction: Nuts are rich in fat, while pulses such as dal are low in fat.

newMisconceptions.name: Every cereal meal needs pulses
newMisconceptions.correction: Animal foods carry all nine essential amino acids, so a meal with egg does not need a pulse for that purpose.

newMisconceptions.name: One protein allowance fits everyone
newMisconceptions.correction: The healthy adult allowance does not cover the higher needs of teens, pregnant women and people who are ill.

newMisconceptions.name: Milk sugar is free sugar
newMisconceptions.correction: The sugar naturally found in milk is not counted as free sugar.

newMisconceptions.name: Dairy drinks cannot contain free sugar
newMisconceptions.correction: Sugar added to a dairy drink counts as free sugar.

newMisconceptions.name: Low fluid leaves pee unchanged
newMisconceptions.correction: Dark yellow pee can be a sign that the body is short of fluid.

newMisconceptions.name: One short night cannot affect focus
newMisconceptions.correction: Losing even one hour of sleep can make it hard to focus.

newMisconceptions.name: Deep sleep fills late night
newMisconceptions.correction: Deep sleep is longer early in the night, while REM sleep grows longer towards morning.

newMisconceptions.name: Chatting signals vigorous effort
newMisconceptions.correction: Moderate effort lets you talk; vigorous effort leaves room for only a few words.

newMisconceptions.name: Ingredient rank compares different packs
newMisconceptions.correction: Ingredient order ranks amounts within a pack; per 100 g values let you compare packs.

newMisconceptions.name: Repeated work only wears muscles out
newMisconceptions.correction: The body adapts to repeated work, so the same load can come to feel easier.

newMisconceptions.name: Muscle building waits until soreness ends
newMisconceptions.correction: Muscle building can stay raised for up to two days after a strength session.

newMisconceptions.name: Protein alone builds muscle
newMisconceptions.correction: Strength work gives the body a signal to use protein for muscle building.

newMisconceptions.name: Early sleep loss hurts sport most
newMisconceptions.correction: In the review, losing the end of the night hurt sport most.

newMisconceptions.name: Short sleep lowers hunger hormone
newMisconceptions.correction: With too little sleep, the hunger hormone rises and the fullness hormone falls.

newMisconceptions.name: Heat symptoms always pass alone
newMisconceptions.correction: Get medical help if heat symptoms last over an hour, get worse or include vomiting.

newMisconceptions.name: Warmups start at full effort
newMisconceptions.correction: A warm-up starts with the activity at a slower speed or lower effort.

newMisconceptions.name: Talking means vigorous effort
newMisconceptions.correction: A chat fits moderate effort; vigorous effort allows only a few words before a breath.

newMisconceptions.name: Habits need changing cues
newMisconceptions.correction: Repeating a small action at the same time each day helps make it a habit.

newMisconceptions.name: A gym makes the habit
newMisconceptions.correction: Repeating a small action at a steady daily cue helps make it a habit.

newMisconceptions.name: Labels omit added sugars
newMisconceptions.correction: Indian labels show added sugars on a separate line from total sugars.

newMisconceptions.name: Added sugar sits outside total sugar
newMisconceptions.correction: Added sugars are part of total sugars, not an extra amount.

newMisconceptions.name: Only drinks need ingredient percentages
newMisconceptions.correction: A mixed food that stresses an ingredient must usually give its percentage.

newMisconceptions.name: Total sugar sets added sugar RDA
newMisconceptions.correction: The added sugar line is the one compared with the daily added sugar reference.

newMisconceptions.name: Milk sugar counts as added
newMisconceptions.correction: Added sugars are only sugars put into a food; its own sugars appear in the total.
